Bloomberg reported that Apple's smart home product plans include devices, lenses and cameras in collaboration with LG. Here are the details.

Apple and LG collaborate on home connected devices

According to Bloomberg, Apple and LG have been working together to develop a series of home connected products, serving as accessories for the upcoming smart home hub, marking the 'official reboot of HomeKit'.

Bloomberg pointed out that the related products include 'doorbells, thermostats ... smart door locks, indoor security cameras, outdoor security cameras and floodlight cameras'.

Gurman noted that although Apple and LG are 'collaborating on these accessories, the products will be launched under the LG brand', and added that 'this Korean company is responsible for manufacturing and product support', and has recently applied for regulatory approval.

It is worth noting that although these products are part of Apple's grand plan to enter the connected home market and are expected to debut alongside the new smart home hub, updated Apple TV and new HomePod mini next week, Bloomberg said 'these products are not expected to hit the consumer market for at least several more months'.

Here is the Bloomberg report:

In recent weeks, LG has applied for regulatory approval for these devices, including filing applications with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and product certification body UL Solutions. The databases of both organisations often contain application documents that reveal the names, specifications, features and design drawings of accessory products. These include products labelled as LG Video Doorbell Wired, LG Floodlight Cam, LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In, LG Indoor Cam Plug-In, LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, LG Smart Thermostat and LG Temperature Sensor. LG has requested that product photos and more detailed information be kept confidential until early next year. The application documents do not mention Apple's involvement.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Scott D.

Well, it's hard to get excited about LG products—after all, this company's TVs record conversations in your living room and send them to who knows where……

Regarding connectivity and standards, the report noted that many devices will support Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread and Matter. The report also noted that the smart door lock is also equipped with UWB (Ultra-Wideband), which can enable functions such as automatic unlocking and other short-range detection capabilities.

Finally, the report noted that for Apple and LG, these products mark a broader expansion of both parties in the smart home market, with Apple hoping to inject new momentum into its home ecosystem:

It is worth emphasising that although this report comes as Apple has just announced the launch of the long-rumoured 'HomePad' smart home hub and other products next week, these LG-made accessories are not expected to hit the consumer market for at least several more months.
